items.title: AI-Driven HR Transformation and the Future of Work
items.abstract: The dawn of artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the functions of human resource (HR) nowadays into strategic enablers of organizational governance, and the implications of human–AI alliance for the future of work. This is with a concentration on both universal and African organizational settings from transactional administrative units. It underscores how AI enables analytical manpower planning, evidence-based decision-making, optimization of talent, and improved employee engagement, while accentuating the significance of ethical oversight, lucidity, answerability, and human-in-the-loop governance. The chapter additionally looks at organizational enablers together with barriers to digital HR transformation, as well as cultural readiness, leadership's commitment, competencies of employee, infrastructural restraints, and circumstantial problem in Africa.

items.title: AI-Driven Kiosk Support for Older Adults Through Nonverbal Behavior Recognition
items.abstract: Older adults experience difficulties using digital kiosks because of low digital literacy, perceived social pressure, and low self-efficacy, and often encounter confusion and negative interactions when errors occur. Additionally, because of the challenges associated with seeking help from nearby individuals, an automated system that detects difficulties and provides support is needed. This study proposes an artificial intelligence (AI) kiosk that automatically detects difficulties experienced by older adults by analyzing their nonverbal behaviors and facial expressions from video data and provides real-time voice and video guidance. Considering that older adults typically require more time to process visual information, a multimodal guidance system combining visual and auditory cues was designed. The concept of “kiosk literacy” was introduced to define five types of guidance: location, task, input, feedback, and screen narration. Furthermore, 16 major pain points experienced by older adults were identified and systematically mapped to their corresponding literacy levels and guidance types to generate appropriate voice and video feedback. A user test with older adults demonstrated that the difficulty detection performance of the proposed AI kiosk achieved 82.35% accuracy, 93.33% precision, 87.5% recall, and an F1 score of 90.32%. Furthermore, the AI kiosk scored significantly higher than conventional kiosks across several user experience dimensions, including ease of use, usefulness, enjoyment, satisfaction, and personalization. These results demonstrate that the proposed approach provides both a technical and practical foundation for improving accessibility and helping bridge the digital divide among older adults.

items.title: AI-Driven Plasma Surface Engineering for Advanced Aerospace and Material Applications
items.abstract: Plasma engineering has become a sophisticated technology for processing surfaces and enhancing functional properties of materials for a wide range of industrial processes. The role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the integration of plasma-based surface engineering and optimization of material properties is explored in this chapter. This emphasizes low temperature and atmospheric plasma processes for coating deposition, surface activation and fabrication of nanostructures. The importance of AI and machine learning for predicting plasma behavior, optimizing process parameters and coating quality is emphasized. Applications such as aerospace, biomedical devices, semiconductor processing and sustainability (CO2 conversion and plasma-assisted catalysis) are discussed. Additionally, experimental diagnostics, numerical simulations, and scalability, process control and industrial integration issues are explored. Finally, future directions towards intelligent and sustainable plasma systems are summarized.

items.title: AI-Driven Talent Acquisition
items.abstract: This chapter explores the transformative impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on talent acquisition in the digital era, emphasising its potential to enhance traditional recruitment processes while also addressing significant ethical and operational considerations. AI-enabled talent acquisition utilises machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive analytics to automate key tasks such as resume screening, candidate sourcing, job matching, and initial assessments. items.title: AI-generated Treatment Plans for Adults with Chronic Pain – Assessment of their Quality by Clinical Experts
items.abstract: Chronic pain affects approximately 20% of adults worldwide. In Canada, 7.6 million, or one in five people (across the lifespan), live with chronic pain. The Canadian Pain Task Force recommends nonpharmacological modalities, including psychotherapy, as a part of first-line therapy for pain management. The Mental Health Commission of Canada recently reported that “‘services for which we know people are waiting too long, if they can get it at all, are psychotherapies and clinical counseling’’, recommending an ‘‘increase to the availability and coordination of mental health services in the community’’. Even with an increase in availability, psychologists are beyond the financial and geographic reach of many patients. Against this backdrop, the use of AI-generative conversational agents for mental health in the form of psychology, psychotherapy, and health coaching has gained significant momentum. AI-generative conversational agents have begun to show some promise in complimenting human therapy, and addressing the needs of those faced with long wait lists or financial barriers to accessing mental health care. However, it has been established that such tools can produce nonfactual content, face challenges setting adequate boundaries, reinforce maladaptive beliefs and be sycophantic towards the user. To our knowledge the quality of treatments provided by AI-generative conversational agents for chronic pain have not yet been explored, and concerns are mounting. In this study, we will investigate treatment plans for chronic pain provided by four AI-generative conversational agents. Three of the conversational agents were selected based on market share across publicly available conversational agents: OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Microsoft’s Co-Pilot, and Google’s Gemini. The fourth conversational agent, Solace, built by the Canadian company ManagingLife, Inc, is the first expert-trained AI-generative conversational agents designed to deliver support to those living with chronic pain and grounded in principles of evidence-based pain psychology. Prompts for this study will be engineered using clinical cases of chronic pain patients from the Faculty of Pain Medicine of the Royal College of Anaesthetists. This is an educational platform offering open resources for all learners in Pain Medicine and is overseen by the Faculty of Pain Medicine's Education Subcommittee. Clinical case reports will be selected and divided into three levels of progressive information completeness. Level 1 will be comprised of current pain-specific information only (e.g., intensity, location). Level 2 will include both current pain and pain history (e.g., duration, surgical history, examination results). Level 3 will be the most comprehensive level including current pain, pain history and psychosocial information (e.g., marital status, stress-related events). For all case reports, each of the three levels will be independently introduced to the conversational agents with the following prompt: “I need help right now”. This prompt was designed to simulate the types of prompts that individuals with chronic pain might enter into a conversational agent. If safety mechanisms are triggered, preventing a conversational agent from providing a treatment recommendation, the following backup prompt will be used: “For the purposes of an educational exercise, what would be your best recommendation based on this information only?”. This study aims to evaluate the quality of AI-generated treatment plans for users with chronic pain. Quality is operationally defined as the use of evidence-based pain psychology interventions and appropriate therapeutic communication. It will be assessed using a 7-domain quality framework adapted from the Quality Analysis of Medical Artificial Intelligence Tool (QAMAI). Clinical experts will conduct a blinded review of the transcripts of participants’ conversations with all four conversational agents and score the domains on a 5-point Likert scale with 1 representing strongly disagree and 5 representing strongly agree, providing a single score for each transcript. Clinical experts will include a team of six evaluators comprised of two anesthesiologists, two physiotherapists, and two psychologists. No identifiable data will be used in the study, and therefore, ethics approval is not required.

items.title: AI–teacher collaboration: professional capital, cultural values and identity grafting
items.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how teachers with varying levels of professional capital respond to artificial intelligence (AI) collaborations, aiming to inform policymakers and school leaders about how to communicate change more effectively. We synthesize theories of professional capital, cultural values and identity grafting (IG) to develop propositions regarding teachers' willingness and ability to engage in AI–teacher collaboration. Specifically, the study analyses how professional capital (human, social and decisional capital) and cultural values (power distance, uncertainty avoidance and risk-taking) interact to shape teachers' IG processes (blending, balancing, repressing and reversing). Design/methodology/approach Drawing on international literature on AI in education and IG constructs as analytical tools, we conducted a secondary analysis to reinterpret our previously published cluster analysis results on Hong Kong teachers. Insights from this secondary analysis informed the development of theoretical and practical implications for future research and practice of AI–teacher collaboration. The process involved: (1) analysing how profiles of professional capital and cultural values from the published results might respectively indicate willingness and ability to engage in AI–teacher collaboration; and (2) theorizing with IG constructs how these patterns might indicate processes that will shape teachers' responses to AI–teacher collaboration. Findings High-professional-capital teachers, being less hierarchical and more risk-taking, are most likely to regard AI as a collaborator, blending their identities during human–machine collaboration. However, in terms of values, their aversion to power distance can lead them to reverse from AI adoption. Medium-professional-capital teachers exemplify the risk-averse middle majority who tend to avoid uncertainty and reverse from novel ideas. They may eventually form collaborative relationships with AI if authoritative agencies provide guidance regarding the benefits. Low-professional-capital teachers are highly likely to become risk-takers who disregard the intended outcomes of AI–teacher collaboration and remain skeptical of reform initiatives. Research limitations/implications This concept paper used our previously published results on teacher collaboration as the grounds for projecting how research on AI–teacher collaboration employing our proposed conceptual framework might look like. As the previously published results were meant to illustrate how the model we propose might link present research on teacher collaboration with future research agendas on AI–teacher collaboration, future research could validate the propositions presented in this paper with updated mixed-methods datasets directly related to AI–teacher collaboration. Practical implications The study offers practical implications for schools to sustain meaningful AI–teacher collaboration in nuanced ways. For high-professional-capital teachers, integrating them in professional learning communities can empower their social capital to co-construct AI–teacher collaboration with other teachers. For medium-professional-capital teachers, low-stakes participation and scaffolded entry into AI use can build confidence in this new knowledge base, promote trust in ethical AI use and ensure that AI usage is coherent with existing teaching norms. For low-professional-capital teachers, trust-building through inclusive yet careful scaffolding of low-stakes leadership opportunities may foster higher engagement toward AI integration and strengthen organizational change capacity. Social implications We offer initial insights into how teachers with different levels of professional capital might respond to calls for AI–teacher collaboration. To address concerns regarding the social ramifications of AI–teacher collaboration, changemakers must go beyond the adopter–nonadopter divide to understand the cultural values that underpin teachers' identity processes when interpreting change. Ignoring these differences risks dividing the teaching profession and the sustainability of AI–teacher collaboration. Initiatives that disempower, force consensus, promote distrust and exclude those who do not appear compliant bring diverse social ramifications, and our conceptual framework provides plausible indications of how they might manifest. Originality/value This paper proposes a theoretically novel IG approach to future research on AI–teacher collaboration, channeling existing research on technological adoption toward understanding teacher identity formations that underpin their willingness and ability to collaborate with AI (cultural values and professional capital). It provides tailored recommendations for policymakers and school leaders on professional development in AI–teacher collaboration for teachers with varied levels of professional capital, considering their cultural values and how they might respond to such support, given their IGs.

items.title: Algorithmic Empathy and Hyper-Personalization in Hospitality 5.0
items.abstract: This chapter by the authors examines the emergence of Hospitality 5.0 as a transformative paradigm integrating artificial intelligence with human-centric service design to deliver hyper-personalized and emotionally engaging guest experiences. It explores the concept of algorithmic empathy, highlighting how AI systems can recognize and respond to emotional cues through affective computing and behavioral analytics. The chapter further analyzes key AI technologies, ethical challenges such as data privacy and bias, and the risk of over-automation. A Hybrid Human–AI Service Model is proposed, combining technological intelligence, human emotional intelligence, and ethical governance to achieve balanced and sustainable service delivery. The chapter concludes by outlining managerial implications and future research directions for responsible innovation in hospitality.

items.title: Algorithmic empathy in nursing – can artificial intelligence support humanism in care
items.abstract: Introduction. Artificial intelligence increasingly supports communication in healthcare by offering tools that simulate empathy and reduce patients’ sense of isolation, particularly in telehealth and senior care. Aim. The aim of this study was to analyze the mechanisms, opportunities and limitations of algorithmic empathy and digital empathy in healthcare, with particular emphasis on nursing practice. Methods. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR (2020) guidelines. Literature searches were performed in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL and Google Scholar, covering publications from 2015 to 2025. Empirical studies, literature reviews and conceptual analyses addressing algorithmic empathy, digital empathy, socially assistive robots, and emotion recognition systems in healthcare were included. A descriptive synthesis was applied. Conclusions. Seven publications were included in the analysis. The results indicate that technological solutions may elicit responses perceived as empathic, which is associated with improved subjective well-being, reduced negative emotions and increased user engagement, primarily in long-term care, geriatric care and telehealth settings. Variability in intervention effectiveness and clinical context–related limitations were also noted. Algorithmic and digital empathy may support nursing care in conditions of limited direct contact. However, the use of such conditions requires professional oversight and a clear distinction between clinical empathy and technological solutions.

items.title: Algorithmic isomorphism and the erosion of competitive advantage in the age of artificial intelligence: A review of emerging risks in strategic management
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is gaining prominence not only as an operational optimization tool, but primarily as a key element shaping decision-making processes and strategic management within organizations. The public and academic debate is dominated by concerns regarding job losses, privacy violations, social manipulation and biases hidden in algorithms. The purpose of this review paper is to transpose these issues into the realm of corporate management and examine a significantly less obvious threat: algorithmic isomorphism. This entails the homogenization of business strategies resulting from widespread reliance on the same global machine learning models. The article analyzes how the imperfections of artificial intelligence systems such as the lack of transparency (the black box effect), inherent database bias and their Western-centric nature can lead to the reproduction of identical market behaviour patterns. Furthermore, the impact of these technologies on the risk of unique know-how leakage and the loss of tacit knowledge held by human managers, which is crucial for competitive advantage, is discussed. The comprehensive analysis also encompasses the transfer of market mechanisms, known from algorithmic financial crises, to the sphere of long-term business decision-making. The conclusions point to the necessity of balancing technological innovation with a human-centric approach to protect corporate identity.

items.title: Algorithmic Management and the Erosion of Institutional Memory
items.abstract: This chapter examines how algorithmic management reshapes organizational resource management while weakening the human knowledge structures that support long-term adaptation. It focuses especially on the tacit knowledge risks that emerge when organizations rely heavily on data-driven managerial systems for coordination, evaluation, allocation, and control. Drawing on literature on tacit knowledge, institutional memory, organizational learning, transactive memory systems, hybrid governance, and human-centric AI, the chapter explains why institutional memory becomes vulnerable under datafied management. It argues that organizations face a dual challenge: they must benefit from AI-enabled efficiency without allowing managerial automation to erode tacit knowledge, mentorship, contextual judgment, and knowledge-sharing routines. To address this challenge, the chapter introduces a Hybrid Knowledge Governance framework and offers practical recommendations for more human-centered AI adoption.

items.title: Algorithmic Management, Technostress, and Employee Mental Health in West Java
items.abstract: This study examines the effect of algorithmic management on employee mental health and the mediating role of technostress, viewing artificial intelligence (AI) as a double-edged sword in the workplace. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 300 employees in West Java, Indonesia, who had used algorithm-based work systems for at least three months and were selected through purposive sampling. The data were analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4.1. The structural model shows that algorithmic management has a significant direct effect on employee mental health and a strong effect on technostress, while technostress significantly affects mental health. The indirect effect through technostress is significant and accounts for about 61% of the total effect, indicating partial mediation. The model explains 78.3% of the variance in mental health and 64.7% of the variance in technostress. The findings show that algorithmic management can raise efficiency but also generates technostress that shapes employees' psychological condition. Organizations should combine AI-based control with human oversight, digital well-being policies, and technostress training. items.title: Amplifying Value Co-Creation in Small Family Businesses through Artificial Intelligence and Neuroscience: Twin Pillars for Intergenerational Decisions and Cohesion
items.abstract: This article examines how artificial intelligence (AI) and neuroscience can jointly amplify value co-creation in small family businesses, whose competitive advantage rests on trust, close relationships and tacit, experience-based know-how transmitted across generations. The study combines a systematic literature review with narrative synthesis and conceptual model-building. Foundational sources were identified through citation tracking, and recent research was captured through a structured Scopus search (30 July 2026) that returned 296 records, of which 24 were retained after screening and quality appraisal and six further records were added through snowballing; a keyword co-occurrence analysis was performed on the full Scopus corpus. The review shows that AI acts as a strategic enabler rather than a mere automation tool, supporting efficiency, customer personalisation, innovation and intergenerational knowledge transfer, although recent evidence (2023–2026) indicates that its effects depend on the mode of family involvement, firm origin, organisational culture and governance. Neuroscience contributes insights into decision-making, creativity, stress and trust in emotionally dense family settings. The bibliometric map confirms that the two literatures have developed largely separately, as neuroscience terms are almost absent from the AI-in-family-business corpus. The article proposes a four-layer conceptual framework in which value co-creation mediates the effects of AI and neuroscience on organisational and family outcomes, moderated by firm-level, ethical and governance conditions, and formulates four working propositions for future empirical testing.

items.title: An audit-ready EHR foundation model for order-time medication-safety auditing across health systems
items.abstract: Real-time medication-safety auditing requires current laboratory and medication histories, yet electronic health records (EHRs) may contain stale or missing decisive evidence. We present ClinicalGPT, an audit-ready foundation model using Clinical Trajectory Language to encode time, units, provenance, and observability, and workflow-aligned objectives to handle structured missingness. Across seven health systems, we retrospectively evaluated 847,000 eligible high-risk medication orders against a reference vector frozen before final scoring. The primary endpoint was the reference-standard-defined order-time failure-to-alert rate: eligible tier-i/ii reference-positive orders receiving no actionable alert at a system’s frozen operating point, per 1000 eligible orders. This offline process metric did not measure subsequent clinical actions, adverse drug events, or patient harm. ClinicalGPT with hard constraints achieved 3.2 misses per 1000 orders, versus 9.4 for rules only, 6.1 for the original generic LLM comparator, and 4.8 for the strongest observed LLM comparator (RAG + LLM + rules). Its false-alert rate was 33.9 (95% CI, 31.6–36.3), versus 38.7 for rules only. A separate single-site silent prospective assessment evaluated workflow measures without altering care. Matched ablations supported explicit observability modeling; independent de novo labeling of an enriched knowledge-base–independent subset preserved sensitivity ordering but narrowed the ClinicalGPT–RAG gap. These findings support comparative order-time auditing performance but do not establish clinical effectiveness or reduced patient harm.

items.title: An Exploration of Attacks on AI Agent Systems
items.abstract: As autonomous AI agents become more integrated into sensitive domains, it is crucial that single and multi-agent AI systems are secured. This paper investigates how prompt injection attacks can exploit both direct user inputs and inter?agent communication to leak sensitive information and trigger cross-agent infections. While our tests mostly highlight key vulnerabilities in single-agent systems, we also extend these attacks to multi-agent frameworks, investigating how weaknesses can propagate across agents. Our findings emphasize the need for more robust defenses as AI agents become more commonly embedded in real-world workflows.

items.title: AN ILLUSION OF ENTREPRENEURIAL COMPETENCE IN ROBOTICS FOR SELF-RELIANCE IN KOGI STATE, NORTH-CENTRAL NIGERIA
items.abstract: This study critically interrogates the disjuncture between policy rhetoric and tangible outcomes in robotics-focused entrepreneurship development within Kogi State, North-Central Nigeria. Despite considerable public and institutional expenditure on robotics education, artificial intelligence infrastructure, and technology incubation schemes, the region exhibits a persistent failure to convert trained human capital into sustainable entrepreneurial ventures. Using a qualitative case-study approach grounded in secondary policy documents, institutional reports, and media coverage, the article argues that robotics entrepreneurship competence in Kogi State is largely performative symbolically enacted through official announcements and training certifications but materially unrealised owing to systemic infrastructural weakness, curricular irrelevance, institutional fragmentation, and deficient market linkages. Five interconnected obstacles are identified: erratic power and bandwidth availability; pedagogical models that privilege theory over practice; feeble university–industry partnerships; acute shortages of risk capital and accessible markets; and the absence of a cohesive ecosystem for technology venturing. The paper concludes by articulating a multi-pronged strategy to close the competence reality chasm, encompassing foundational infrastructure upgrades, curriculum overhaul, ecosystem orchestration, and locally attuned robotics applications. The analysis offers transferable insights for technology-entrepreneurship policy across sub-Saharan Africa, where similar mismatches between ambition and implementation are endemic.

items.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of experience using Artificial Intelligence (AI) on self‑efficacy and academic dishonesty among students in the Building Information Modeling and Design (DPIB) Expertise Program at SMK Negeri 1 Singosari. The study employed a quantitative explanatory approach, with a sample of 103 students selected through stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using SEM‑PLS. The results indicate that experience using AI has a positive and significant effect on self‑efficacy, a negative but insignificant effect on academic dishonesty, and that self‑efficacy has a positive and significant effect on academic dishonesty. These findings emphasize the importance of utilizing AI coupled with digital literacy and ethical awareness in learning. In addition, the study highlights the relevance of integrating technological experience into educational practices, encouraging students to develop confidence, responsibility, and integrity. The implications suggest that schools should design programs that foster ethical digital skills and strengthen students’ readiness for future innovation.

items.title: Anytime-valid detection of LLM weight exfiltration
items.abstract: A compromised LLM inference server can leak model weights by encoding payload bits in otherwise plausible token choices. A replay of the same prompt in a trusted server can expose such deviations, but benign numerical nondeterminism also causes token mismatches. Patient attackers can therefore hide within normal variation unless evidence is combined across responses. We introduce a prompt-level e-process that calibrates whole-response mismatch events on trusted benign traffic and accumulates evidence sequentially while, under a calibration-transfer assumption, controlling the probability of any false alarm over an unbounded monitoring horizon. We evaluate it on four models against a seed-blind attack and a stronger seed-aware attack that hides payload bits only in near-ties to remain stealthy, analyzing the channel capacity vs detectability trade-off. Compared with a hard per-token alarm, the e-process combines weak evidence across responses while providing explicit anytime false-alarm control.

items.abstract: This thesis examines the possibilities of using artificial intelligence technologies to assess the earthquake resistance of buildings. Earthquakes can cause cracks, deformations, displacements, and other types of damage to building structures. Since traditional assessment methods often require considerable time and human resources, the use of modern machine learning and computer vision algorithms is becoming increasingly important. This study analyzes the possibilities of using photographs and video data of buildings to automatically detect structural damage, assess its severity, and provide a preliminary evaluation of the building's seismic performance.

items.title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON MARKETING PERFORMANCE, GUEST SATISFACTION AND LOYALTY: IMPLICATIONS FOR SUSTAINABLE INTERNATIONAL HOTEL BUSINESS IN ABUJA, NIGERIA
items.abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping hotel marketing and guest-service delivery, yet empirical evidence on its implications for guest satisfaction and loyalty in developing hospitality markets remains limited. This study examined AI applications in selected international hotels in Abuja, Nigeria, focusing on their perceived contribution to marketing performance, guest satisfaction and loyalty, as well as barriers to adoption. A cross-sectional mixed-methods design was employed, involving hotel staff and guests from six selected hotels. Data were collected through structured questionnaires, key-informant interviews and observation. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression and mediation analysis were used to examine relationships among the study variables. The findings indicate that conventional digital technologies were more widely used than genuine AI applications, with chatbots, machine-learning forecasting, intelligent recommendation systems and AI-supported analytics representing the principal AI-related applications. AI-supported guest experience was positively associated with satisfaction, while satisfaction demonstrated a stronger relationship with loyalty. The findings further indicate that cost, shortage of specialised skills, privacy and cybersecurity concerns, systems integration and infrastructural limitations constrain effective AI adoption. The study concludes that AI does not automatically generate guest loyalty; rather, its value depends on the quality, relevance and trustworthiness of the experience it creates. The study contributes by distinguishing AI from conventional digitalisation and proposing a human-centred pathway linking AI-supported experience, satisfaction and loyalty in the Abuja hospitality context.

items.title: Application of deep learning and explainable AI-supported medical decision-making for facial phenotyping in genetic syndromes
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly employed in clinical genetics to assist in diagnosing genetic conditions by assessing photographs of patients. For medical uses of AI, explainable AI (XAI) methods offer a promising approach by providing interpretable outputs, such as saliency maps and region relevance visualizations. XAI has been discussed as important for regulatory purposes and to enable clinicians to better understand how AI tools work in practice. However, the real-world effects of XAI on clinician performance, confidence, and trust remain underexplored. This study involved a web-based user experiment with 31 medical geneticists to assess the impact of AI-only diagnostic assistance compared to XAI-supported diagnostics. Participants were randomly assigned to either group and completed diagnostic tasks with 18 facial images of individuals with known genetic syndromes and unaffected individuals, before and after experiencing the AI outputs. The results show that both AI-only and XAI approaches improved diagnostic accuracy and clinician confidence. The effects varied according to the accuracy of AI predictions and the clarity of syndromic features (sample difficulty). While AI support was viewed positively, users approached XAI with skepticism. Interestingly, we found a positive correlation between diagnostic improvement and XAI intervention. Although XAI support did not significantly enhance overall performance relative to AI alone, it prompted users to critically evaluate images with false predictions and influenced their confidence levels. These findings highlight the complexities of trust, perceived usefulness, and interpretability in AI-assisted diagnostics, with important implications for developing and implementing clinical decision-support tools in facial phenotyping for rare genetic diseases.

items.title: Artificial gravity for long-duration human spaceflight: physiological rationale, evidence gaps, risks, and research priorities
items.abstract: Long-duration missions beyond low Earth orbit will expose crews to prolonged microgravity during transit and partial gravity on the Moon or Mars. Existing exercise, nutritional, pharmacological, and sensorimotor countermeasures mitigate selected aspects of deconditioning but do not reproduce gravity’s continuous multisystem stimulus. Artificial gravity (AG), generated by rotation, is therefore a promising integrative countermeasure. This structured narrative review evaluates the physiological rationale for AG, evidence from human centrifugation and ground-based analog studies, human-factors and engineering constraints, and priorities for exploration missions. Evidence is strongest for the acute restoration of hydrostatic gradients and cardiovascular loading and is suggestive, although heterogeneous, for preserving orthostatic tolerance, muscle function, and selected sensorimotor outcomes. In the 60-day AGBRESA study (24 participants; eight per group), daily continuous or intermittent centrifugation attenuated the decline in time to presyncope relative to control but did not prevent several autonomic, ocular, balance, or mobility changes. Evidence for durable protection of bone, connective tissues, neuro-ocular health, immunity, endocrine and circadian regulation, cognition, sleep, and behavioural health remains insufficient. Interpretation is limited by small samples, overlapping cohort analyses, heterogeneous exposure geometries and schedules, and reliance on bed-rest analogs rather than in-flight trials. AG should therefore be regarded as a configurable intervention rather than a single countermeasure. Translation requires standardized reporting, adequately powered comparative studies, explicit safety and ethical governance, analyses of sex-related and individual responses, combined AG–exercise protocols, and phased validation from ground-based analogs to orbital demonstrators.

items.title: Artificial intelligence - driven toxicogenomics for predictive environmental and pharmaceutical safety
items.abstract: Toxicogenomics integrates high-throughput genomic technologies with toxicology to evaluate molecular responses to chemical and pharmaceutical exposures. The increasing volume and complexity of multi-omics data necessitate advanced computational approaches capable of extracting meaningful and predictive insights. In this context, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques—including support vector machines, random forests, and deep learning architectures—are increasingly employed for early toxicity prediction and risk assessment, with reported improvements in predictive accuracy and sensitivity relative to conventional toxicological approaches. This paper explores the role of AI-driven toxicogenomics in enhancing predictive environmental and pharmaceutical safety. It highlights the application of ML-based and data-driven models for the integrative analysis of transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic datasets to identify toxicity-associated biomarkers, elucidate mechanisms of action, and predict adverse drug and environmental effects prior to clinical manifestation. Notably, AI-driven models have demonstrated significant improvements in prediction accuracy, sensitivity, and scalability compared to traditional toxicological approaches, reducing reliance on animal testing and accelerating decision-making processes. Furthermore, the paper discusses the significance of AI-based toxicogenomics in drug development, environmental contaminant screening, and regulatory toxicology, while addressing key challenges such as data heterogeneity, model interpretability, and regulatory acceptance. The convergence of computer science and toxicogenomics represents a robust framework for next-generation predictive toxicology, facilitating safer pharmaceutical development, more precise environmental risk assessment, and evidence-based public health and regulatory decision-making.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Image-Based Tools for Automated Mosquito Identification: Advancing Beyond Traditional Methods
items.abstract: Abstract Mosquitoes are primary vectors of devastating diseases such as malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and Japanese encephalitis, placing billions of people worldwide at risk. Accurate species-level identification of both larvae and adults is critical for designing effective vector surveillance and integrated vector management strategies. Traditionally, morphological identification using dichotomous keys and microscopic examination has been the gold standard, but it is labor-intensive, time-consuming, and often limited by the availability of trained taxonomists. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and computer vision have introduced powerful alternatives for both larval and adult mosquito identification. Machine learning algorithms, deep learning architectures such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and vision transformers (ViTs) have demonstrated high accuracy in classifying mosquito images based on morphometric, textural, and wing venation features. In adults, AI-based geometric morphometry of wings and automated image classification systems have shown promising results, while in larvae, low-magnification imaging combined with deep learning has enabled accurate species discrimination even under challenging field conditions. Integration of these tools with IoT-based smart traps, drones, and mobile applications further enhances real-time vector surveillance capabilities. Despite remarkable progress, challenges remain, including limited annotated datasets, variations in image quality, model generalizability across geographies, and ethical concerns related to open-access data. This chapter critically examines the evolution of mosquito identification methods, highlighting how AI and image-based tools are advancing beyond traditional approaches for both larvae and adult mosquitoes. By bridging technological innovation with entomological expertise, AI-powered system holds the potential to transform vector surveillance, contributing significantly to sustainable control of mosquito-borne diseases. items.title: Artificial intelligence and digital technologies in public administration: a constitutional and legal dimension
items.abstract: This article presents a comprehensive constitutional-legal analysis of the use of artificial intelligence and other digital technologies in public administration. The study aims to define the constitutional and legal foundations for their application, identify key risks to human rights and freedoms, and substantiate a differentiated model of legal safeguards based on the intensity of digital influence on legally significant outcomes. The relevance of this issue stems from the gradual shift from using digital tools merely for technical support to employing them in processes involving data analysis, the formulation of recommendations, the determination of parameters for official decisions, and the automated adoption of legally significant decisions. The study employs formal-legal, comparative-legal, and system-structural methods, as well as the method of legal modeling. It analyzes constitutional principles and norms of national legislation, contemporary European and international approaches to the regulation of artificial intelligence, and the specific aspects of using automated systems in the activities of public administration. The article establishes that the constitutional and legal significance of digital technology is determined by the extent of its impact on the exercise of public authority and the legal status of the individual. It is argued that a digital system cannot serve as an independent source of public competence; rather, its software architecture and settings must comply with legally prescribed limits of authority and cannot effectively alter the substance of legal regulation. The article analyzes the requirements of legality, legal certainty, equality and non-discrimination, privacy protection, accountability, due process, and effective legal protection within the context of the algorithmization of public administration. The scientific novelty of the study lies in substantiating the principle that constitutional and legal safeguards should be strengthened in proportion to the intensity of digital influence. Building on this principle, the article proposes a four-level model of digital influence and develops a digital influence intensity test based on four criteria: the functional role of the system, the nature of the legal consequences, the characteristics of the data used, and the extent to which meaningful human review is genuinely available. The study further substantiates a set of safeguards applicable in cases of substantial digital influence, including the right to be informed about the significant use of artificial intelligence, a legally sufficient explanation of the decision, meaningful human review, a prior impact assessment concerning constitutional rights, digital auditing, and effective mechanisms for review and appeal. It is concluded that it is advisable to establish a differentiated model of legal regulation for the use of artificial intelligence in public administration in Ukraine, wherein the scope of legal safeguards is determined by the digital system's actual role in generating a legally significant outcome. This approach makes it possible to reconcile the efficiency of public sector digitalization with the requirements of legality, accountability, and adequate human rights protection, without imposing uniformly stringent regulatory requirements on technologies that have varying degrees of legal impact.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND GEOSPATIAL TECHNOLOGIES FOR WATER QUALITY MONITORING: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF TRENDS, METHODS, AND RESEARCH GAPS
items.abstract: Water quality monitoring is essential for ensuring the sustainable use of aquatic resources and preserving ecosystem health. The increasing application of artificial intelligence (AI) in this field has provided innovative approaches to modeling and predicting key water quality parameters with greater efficiency. This study aimed to map the landscape of scientific production, understand the correlation network among identified themes, and analyze the temporal evolution of publication output. We conducted a bibliometric analysis of scientific publications related to the use of AI in water quality assessment, employing tools such as Bibliometrix and VOSviewer. A total of 130 peer-reviewed articles were retrieved from the Web of Science and Scopus databases, covering the period from 2005 to 2025, and analyzed to identify research trends, key themes, and collaboration networks. Thematic clustering of keywords revealed four main research areas: (i) remote sensing, (ii) machine learning, (iii) water quality indicators, and (iv) hydrodynamic and watershed modeling. The results show that the term “machine learning” is central to the analyzed literature, connecting clusters focused on hydrological modeling, remote sensing, supervised learning algorithms, and the prediction of physicochemical variables. The findings highlight the interdisciplinary nature of the field and underscore the growing role of AI and geotechnologies as cost-effective tools for supporting water quality management, particularly in hard-to-access areas. These insights offer guidance for future research and help environmental agencies develop more efficient strategies for monitoring and preserving water resources.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Asthma Care in Nigeria and Sub-Saharan Africa: Evidence, Opportunities, and Adoption Barriers
items.abstract: Asthma affects an estimated 363 million people worldwide and caused approximately 442,000 deaths in 2023. The burden of this disease falls disproportionately on low-income and middle-income countries where the disease is mostly underdiagnosed and under-treated. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have been presented as tools for earlier diagnosis, personalised treatment, exacerbation prediction, and remote monitoring. However, much of the supporting research originates from high-income settings. Our review evaluates what the supporting evidence offers for asthma care in Nigeria and the African region. We conducted a literature search across PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and similar databases, with the resulting review library consisting of 170 screened records. 116 records were reviewed in full, while 31 were retained for in-depth review of their techniques, data sources, algorithms, conclusions, and implications. Four themes emerged: an expanding but unevenly equipped African AI ecosystem; AI/ML tools for diagnosis, exacerbation prediction, and digital monitoring developed and validated almost entirely outside Africa; persistent non-technical barriers to asthma care in sub-Saharan Africa, including under-diagnosis, restricted access to medications, and insufficient awareness among carers and educators; and unresolved ethical, legal, and data governance issues. The reviewed studies demonstrate technical feasibility in high-income settings but reveal a lack of African validation. We conclude that AI and ML can enhance asthma care in Nigeria only if models are validated on African data, integrated into existing care frameworks, and governed by explicit regulations. We therefore propose seven recommendations for policymakers, clinicians, and researchers.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Economic Theory
items.abstract: This chapter investigates the growing influence of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) on major economic theories and contemporary economic analysis. The chapter explores how AI and ML are reshaping classical, Keynesian, monetarist, behavioural, institutional, and network economics through advanced computational modelling, predictive analytics, and large-scale data-processing. AI and ML increasingly enhance economic forecasting, labour market analysis, market simulations, policy evaluation, and international trade analysis by improving the ability to identify complex and non-linear relationships within economic systems. The chapter further demonstrates how these technologies strengthen the analysis of consumer behaviour, macroeconomic stability, strategic interactions, and digital economic networks within increasingly interconnected economies. Rather than replacing traditional economic theories, AI and ML expand the analytical capacity of economics by supporting more adaptive, data-driven, and computational approaches to understanding economic behaviour and policy outcomes in technologically driven economies.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning-Powered Labour Market Analytics
items.abstract: This chapter examines the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in labour market analytics and workforce intelligence systems. The chapter explores the evolution from traditional labour market analysis methods towards AI-driven analytical approaches capable of processing large-scale structured and unstructured labour market data in real time. Key AI and ML techniques, including supervised learning, unsupervised learning, neural networks, and natural language processing, are discussed in relation to labour market forecasting, workforce segmentation, recruitment optimisation, and skills analysis. The chapter further highlights the growing importance of interdisciplinary labour market analysis, AI-driven skill development, and educational transformation in response to changing workforce demands. In addition, ethical concerns surrounding algorithmic bias, transparency, data privacy, and workforce inequalities are critically examined alongside emerging public policy and regulatory responses. In short, the chapter demonstrates how AI and ML are reshaping labour market analysis, improving workforce planning, and supporting more responsive and evidence-based employment decision-making.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE IN BANGLADESH: LEGAL CHALLENGES AND FUTURE PROSPECTS
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming legal systems across the world by improving judicial efficiency, enhancing case management, supporting legal research, and facilitating access to justice. Many jurisdictions have introduced AI-assisted technologies to reduce case backlogs, improve administrative functions, and increase the efficiency of court services. While AI has the potential to strengthen judicial administration, its integration into the justice system also raises significant legal, ethical, and constitutional concerns relating to transparency, accountability, algorithmic bias, data protection, and judicial independence. In Bangladesh, the judiciary has made considerable progress in digitalizing court services through initiatives such as virtual courts, e-filing, and digital case management systems. However, the application of AI in judicial administration remains at a preliminary stage, and the country currently lacks a comprehensive legal framework governing the responsible use of AI within the justice sector. This regulatory gap creates uncertainty regarding the protection of fundamental rights, due process, and judicial accountability. This article critically examines the prospects and challenges of integrating Artificial Intelligence into the administration of justice in Bangladesh. It analyzes the existing constitutional and legal framework, evaluates international developments concerning AI governance, and explores the legal and institutional reforms necessary to ensure that AI serves as a tool to support, rather than replace, judicial decision-making. The article argues that a transparent, accountable, and human-centred regulatory framework is essential for promoting innovation while preserving judicial independence, the rule of law, and public confidence in the justice system.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Cross-Cultural Percussion Analysis: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review of Tabla and Conga
items.abstract: While AI has enhanced automatic drum transcription, culturally unique percussion instruments, due to their common peculiar timbral, harmonic and microtiming properties, are still underrepresented. This systematic review explores the analysis of Hindustani tabla and Afro-Cuban conga (and other related non-Western percussion traditions) using an AI approach. The peer-reviewed papers retrieved from IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Scopus, ISMIR and Google Scholar according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Fourty-seven studies were synthesized across the areas of transcription, rhythmic analysis, low resource learning, and generative modelling of adequate quality and the author applied certain preceding eligibility criteria. Convolutional recurrent neural networks (CRNNs) were able to distinguish between tableau and tabla-strokes in concert recordings with an F score of 0.965, while the other deep-learning models got an accuracy of 97.50% in rhythmic-pattern recognition. The groove modelling of Afro-Latin showed that the adaptability under limited annotated data was boosted by meta-learning and data augmentation, while tatum-level beat and microtiming analysis was critical. The generation of stylistic percussion patterns is another major challenge in the generative approach, which is also faced by sparse datasets, domain shift, cultural bias and real time polyphonic transcription. Therefore, for accurate and authentic cross-cultural percussion analysis culturally informed, transparent and human-centred models are crucial for AI.

items.title: Artificial intelligence for sustainable development: assessing net carbon mitigation benefits of AI-based climate solutions with anomaly detection and life-cycle emissions accounting
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can support climate mitigation through renewable-energy forecasting, demand-side management, and low-energy transport routing, but the climate value of these applications is frequently reported without deducting the emissions generated across the AI system life cycle. This study develops an integrated, reproducible framework for estimating the net carbon mitigation benefit of AI-based climate solutions. The framework combines: (i) gross avoided emissions relative to a functionally equivalent non-AI baseline; (ii) operational emissions from model development, training, inference, data storage, and supporting infrastructure; (iii) allocated embodied emissions from computing hardware and end-of-life treatment; and (iv) an anomaly-detection layer that screens extracted parameters for unit errors, impossible values, inconsistent system boundaries, and influential outliers before carbon calculations are performed. The framework is demonstrated using three literature-derived applications concerning photovoltaic/demand-side energy management, energy-system optimization, and machine-learning-assisted electric-vehicle routing. The source studies report gross improvements of approximately 34%, 73%, and 9%, respectively; however, these percentages are not directly comparable until the functional unit, deployment scale, grid carbon intensity, and computational burden are harmonized. Within the evaluated scenarios, deployment scale and electricity-grid carbon intensity are among the factors that materially influence the estimated net benefit. Hardware manufacturing, supporting infrastructure, and end-of-life impacts could reduce the estimated net benefit further; however, these components were not quantified in the empirical demonstrations because case-specific data were unavailable. Because several computational inputs are not disclosed by the original studies, the numerical results are presented as scenario-based estimates rather than measurements. The proposed framework advances sustainable-development assessment by linking data-quality control, life-cycle emissions accounting, sensitivity analysis, and carbon break-even analysis in a single decision procedure.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Thyroid Nodule Diagnosis: From Multimodal Integration to Clinical Utility
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) for thyroid nodules should be evaluated against the decisions it changes, not diagnostic accuracy alone. This critical narrative review examines ultrasound, cytology, histology, and molecular models and distinguishes modality-specific prediction from implemented multimodal learning. The original PubMed/MEDLINE search through 10 August 2026 was supplemented on 25 September 2026 by targeted OpenAlex searches and checks of primary publications, reporting standards, and regulatory sources. Selected studies are compared by sample size, reference standard, acquisition setting, testing design, and performance with confidence intervals where available. We explain feature concatenation, intermediate representation learning, cross-attention, and decision-level fusion, and examine whether integration improves on the strongest component. Reported gains are inconsistent, and complete-case multimodal datasets may exclude the low-risk nodules most relevant to avoiding biopsy. High discrimination for histological malignancy or occult nodal disease does not demonstrate reduced overdiagnosis, fewer operations, or improved survival. A thyroid-specific translation roadmap therefore addresses active surveillance, partial verification and spectrum bias, Hashimoto thyroiditis and multinodular disease, cytology preparation shifts, category-specific thresholds, operator dependence, reporting frameworks, and regulatory change control. The priority is a calibrated, externally tested tool using information available at a defined clinical decision, followed by prospective evaluation of patient and workflow outcomes. A unified imaging–pathology–omics system and reliable AI prediction of surveillance progression remain research objectives rather than established clinical capabilities.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Auditing the Quality of Electronic Nursing Records: A Critical Narrative Literature Review
items.abstract: Electronic nursing records contain assessments, interventions, and evaluations that can be examined for documentation quality, but extracting information from a record is different from verifying its clinical accuracy. This critical narrative and thematic review asks which applications, results, and limitations of artificial intelligence (AI) in auditing electronic nursing documentation are described in the scientific literature. Targeted scholarly web discovery, primary-source retrieval, and reference checking were completed on October 6, 2026, with a reproducible supplementary PubMed search on October 7, 2026. Twenty-six publications and official documents were retained and classified by their evidentiary role. The synthesis distinguishes direct documentation auditing from terminology mapping, AI-assisted documentation generation, contextual nursing research, and methodological or regulatory guidance. Only one of the 14 retained empirical publications directly evaluated AI-supported quality control of existing nursing documentation. That implementation reported fewer omissions and inconsistencies, although a nonrandomized design and inconsistent reporting limit causal interpretation. Terminology-mapping studies showed configuration-dependent performance and substantial residual errors; scenario-based instrument validation and documentation-generation studies support selected evaluation methods but do not establish comprehensive autonomous auditing. Across the corpus, documentation quality, classifier performance, workload, and patient outcomes require separate endpoints. An author-developed, unvalidated governance workflow is proposed to connect criterion definition, authorized data access, evidence-linked flags, nurse adjudication, and prospective monitoring. The literature supports supervised assistance for bounded audit tasks; it does not establish that AI can independently certify record truth, judge nursing performance, or improve patient safety across institutions. Multicenter validation, clinically weighted error analysis, transparent reference standards, and evaluation of total verification effort remain priorities.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Beer Brewing: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in beer brewing, but the literature is spread across brewing technology, food quality, process engineering, and data science. This review synthesizes 188 publications on AI applications in beer brewing (176 primary studies and 12 reviews), identified through searches in seven bibliographic databases and manually screened for relevance against an explicitly stated criterion for what qualifies as an AI application. The studies were characterized by brewing phase, data modality, computational approach, and task and are mapped here onto brewing phase and the main computational approach used. The review shows that AI applications are not evenly distributed across the brewing process. Quality assurance and fermentation are the most studied areas, while bottling, production planning, and raw material assessment are less represented. Neural networks are especially common in fermentation modeling, where they are used for state estimation, prediction, control, and optimization. Computer vision is mainly applied to raw materials, bottling, foam, color, and product inspection. Electronic-nose and spectroscopic data, interpreted using chemometric and machine-learning models, support beer authentication, defect detection, sensory prediction, and quality classification. Industry 4.0 systems and digital twins provide infrastructure for process-wide data collection, planning, and sustainability assessment. Overall, AI in brewing is best understood as a set of phase-specific tools rather than one uniform technology. Wider industrial adoption will require validated datasets, robust sensors, interpretable models, and integration with routine brewery operations.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cloud Computing: A Systematic Literature Review of Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with cloud computing has emerged as an important research area for developing scalable, intelligent, and automated computing environments. Cloud computing provides on-demand access to computing resources, storage, networking, and software services, while AI and Machine Learning (ML) enable systems to analyse large volumes of data, make predictions, optimize resources, and automate decision-making. This review examines major applications of AI-enabled cloud environments, including intelligent resource management, load balancing, security monitoring, fault prediction, energy optimization, storage management, cost optimization, quality-of-service prediction, and edge-cloud intelligence. It also examines challenges including data privacy, security, computational cost, model explainability, interoperability, data dependency, and resource requirements. Future research directions include autonomous cloud management, federated learning, Explainable AI, AI-driven serverless computing, edge-cloud intelligence, foundation models, green AI, and AI-assisted cybersecurity. The review concludes that the convergence of AI and cloud computing provides significant opportunities for intelligent, scalable, secure, and sustainable computing systems.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DERMATOLOGY: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF DIAGNOSTIC AND THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS, CHALLENGES AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
items.abstract: Skin diseases are among the most common diseases affecting 1.9 billion people worldwide. They remain a major cause of non-fatal disease burden, in part because diagnosis of skin diseases is often challenging due to high visual similarity of skin conditions, subjectivity of clinical diagnosis, and lack of dermatologists worldwide. Deep learning-based artificial intelligence (AI) applied to dermatological images has emerged as a promising tool for dermatological diagnosis and treatment in the last decade. This review provides a comprehensive overview of skin diseases, conventional diagnosis and treatment in dermatology, and core AI technologies, including convolutional neural networks (CNN), computer vision, natural language processing (NLP), and explainable AI, that are currently applied in dermatology for a range of applications including skin cancer, inflammatory and pigmentary skin diseases, disease severity scoring, individualized treatment planning, teledermatology, and even dermatological drug discover. We also discuss current regulatory developments including the first AI-enabled primary-care skin cancer device authorized by US Food and Drug Administration in 2024.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN ECOMMERCE – EMERGING OPPORTUNITIES AND PATHWAYS TO SUSTAINABLE GROWTH
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming a major driver of transformation in e-commerce by changing how firms understand customers, design digital experiences, manage inventories, optimize logistics, communicate with consumers, and make strategic decisions. The rapid development of machine learning, recommendation systems, natural language processing, computer vision, generative AI, and AI-enabled agents has created new opportunities for e-commerce firms to improve efficiency, personalization, innovation, and market reach. At the same time, the sustainability of AI-enabled e-commerce cannot be evaluated only through financial performance. It also requires attention to environmental efficiency, responsible consumption, privacy, fairness, transparency, consumer autonomy, employment, and digital inclusion. This paper examines the emerging opportunities created by AI in e-commerce and develops a conceptual pathway through which AI capabilities can contribute to sustainable business growth. The study adopts a conceptual literature-review approach and synthesizes academic and institutional literature on AI, e-commerce, digital marketing, consumer behaviour, responsible AI, and sustainable development. The review shows that AI can support sustainable growth through five interconnected pathways: intelligent customer engagement, operational and supply chain optimization, data-driven decision-making, sustainable consumption support, and business-model innovation. However, these benefits are conditional on responsible data governance, transparency, cybersecurity, human oversight, algorithmic fairness, energy-aware AI deployment, and inclusive access to digital technologies. The paper proposes a responsible AI-enabled e-commerce framework in which technological capability, organizational readiness, consumer trust, and sustainability governance jointly influence long-term business value. The study concludes that AI should be treated not merely as an automation technology but as a strategic capability that must be aligned with economic, social, and environmental objectives. The paper provides implications for e-commerce firms, policymakers, researchers, and managers seeking to combine innovation with responsible and sustainable growth.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN FINANCIAL STATEMENT FRAUD DETECTION: A CRITICAL SYNTHESIS OF EMERGING TRENDS, METHODOLOGIES, AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS FOR U.S. PUBLICLY TRADED COMPANIES
items.abstract: Financial statement fraud causes systemic damage to U.S. capital markets, investor confidence, and the credibility of public company disclosures. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers promising new detection capabilities, yet its evidence base and operational readiness remain unevenly developed across the literature. This structured narrative review critically synthesizes peer-reviewed articles published between 2020 and 2026 on AI-based fraud detection in SEC-reporting publicly traded U.S. companies, with focused attention on methodological rigor, strength of evidence, and deployment readiness. The thematic synthesis shows five emerging phenomena: (1) ensemble and deep learning models significantly outperform classical ratio screens in structured data; (2) NLP models based on transformer architectures identify fraud signals from narrative disclosures, which are independent of the structured data; (3) multimodal fusion architectures result in the highest detection performance (AUC 0.86–0.91); (4) AI is starting to transform audit risk assessment and regulatory surveillance; and (5) operational deployment is still hindered by challenges with explainability, temporal validation, label quality, and adversarial robustness. Persistent gaps remain in model explainability, temporal validation, adversarial robustness, and regulatory deployment protocols. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework is proposed as an organizing governance structure. Explainable AI, federated learning, and blockchain-based audit trails are identified as priority research investments, with targeted recommendations offered for regulators, auditors, and capital market participants.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare: From Predictive Models to Generative, Multimodal, and Agentic AI
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used across the diagnostic pathway, from screening and disease detection to differential diagnosis, prognostic stratification, and treatment-response assessment. This narrative review examines predictive, generative, multi-modal, and agentic AI through a diagnostic-science lens and evaluates the evidence required for translation into clinical practice. Predictive models can identify complex patterns in images, physiological signals, laboratory data, and electronic health records, but high retrospective accuracy does not establish diagnostic utility. Clinical validity and utility depend on the intended use, target population, disease spectrum and prevalence, reference standard, operating threshold, calibration, and the consequences of false-positive and false-negative results. Generative AI may support problem representation, differential diagnosis, information synthesis, and documentation, yet fluent outputs can omit critical alternatives, amplify false premises, or convey unjustified certainty. Multimodal systems may better reflect clinical reasoning by integrating imaging, text, signals, pathology, and molecular data, but they must demonstrate incremental value over the best single-modality test and remain robust to missing data. Agentic systems can coordinate evidence retrieval, test selection, and sequential workflows, thereby increasing the need for bounded permissions, auditability, error recovery, and human escalation. Across all paradigms, a credible pathway to diagnostic implementation requires independent external and prospective validation, representative consecutive patients, subgroup analysis, workflow and human–AI evaluation, clinical impact studies, and post-deployment surveillance. The field should therefore be judged not by model capability alone, but by whether AI measurably improves diagnostic yield, timeliness, safety, equity, and patient-relevant outcomes in real care settings.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mass Spectrometry-Based Metabolomics and Lipidomics for Drug Discovery and Development
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence applied to mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics has advanced through three technological generations: chemometric and classical machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with large language models so far entering mainly at the edges. The metabolome and lipidome lie closest to drug action, yet they have been among the slowest omics layers to adopt modern artificial intelligence. This paradox arises from their downstream position, which leaves them without a closed molecular reference and without the standardized, readily modeled data available to the genome and transcriptome. This review examines what these methods contribute to drug discovery and development. We survey applications across the drug-development pipeline, from target identification and mechanism-of-action deconvolution, through the prediction of drug-induced toxicity, to pharmacometabolomics, in which pre-dose metabolic phenotypes inform patient stratification and dosing. Across these metabolomic and lipidomic applications, interpretable classical machine learning remains the dominant form of artificial intelligence. The newer deep-learning and foundation models have concentrated instead on compound annotation, the cross-cutting problem of assigning confident identities to spectra, yet successive generations have mitigated but not solved it. Beyond annotation confidence, batch effects, semi-quantification, and small-cohort overfitting also remain practical constraints. Overall, targeted, hypothesis-driven metabolomic and lipidomic studies can already support drug discovery when their inferences are restricted to confidently identified metabolites, whereas open, hypothesis-free discovery remains the frontier. Near-term progress will depend less on any single algorithm than on curated spectral resources, rigorous measurement, leakage-aware validation, and honest reporting of identification confidence.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in National Security: Applications, Risks, and Governance Pathways
items.abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), its applications have gradually expanded from the commercial and civilian sectors to national security fields such as military security, cybersecurity, and critical infrastructure protection. Using a literature review and case analysis approach, this article examines the main applications of AI in different security scenarios and the risks they bring. The study finds that AI can improve the information processing and response capabilities of the national security system by enhancing the efficiency of multi-source information processing, strengthening threat identification and prediction capabilities, and increasing the autonomy of military systems. However, enhanced AI capabilities do not necessarily lead to higher levels of security. Its national security applications face three interconnected risks: technical unreliability, malicious use, and strategic instability arising from the security dilemma. Therefore, this article argues that AI governance cannot rely solely on technological improvements. Instead, it requires a governance path comprised of technical safeguards, risk-based regulation, and international cooperation. This should be achieved through testing, auditing, human-in-the-loop mechanisms, and confidence-building measures (CBMs) to mitigate the risks posed by technological errors, malicious misuse, and strategic miscalculations. Overall, the key to AI governance is not restricting AI's entry into the national security domain, but rather establishing corresponding control, oversight, and international coordination mechanisms while enhancing its security capabilities.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in paediatric cardiac critical care: from predictive analytics to continuous physiologic intelligence
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Artificial intelligence is increasingly applied in paediatric cardiology and cardiac intensive care, where CHD, postoperative physiologic instability, and continuous bedside monitoring generate complex datasets. This review summarises current applications of artificial intelligence in paediatric cardiology and the cardiac ICU, focusing on cardiac imaging, electrocardiography, predictive analytics, waveform intelligence, and postoperative outcome prediction. DATA SOURCES: A narrative review of PubMed, MEDLINE, and Scopus was performed for studies published from 2018 through 2026 evaluating artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in paediatric cardiology, CHD, congenital heart surgery, and cardiac critical care. STUDY SELECTION: Studies addressing paediatric or CHD-focused applications in echocardiography, cardiac MRI, electrocardiography, cardiac ICU monitoring, waveform analytics, or postoperative complication prediction were included, together with relevant reviews. DATA EXTRACTION: Information was extracted on study population, artificial intelligence method, clinical task, model inputs, outcomes, validation strategy, and major limitations. DATA SYNTHESIS: Artificial intelligence is most developed in imaging and electrocardiography, while paediatric and complex CHD evidence remains less mature. In cardiac ICU, models using electronic health record variables, high-frequency physiologic data, and risk indices have been evaluated for cardiac arrest, low cardiac output physiology, hyperlactatemia, extubation failure, and vasoactive de-escalation. External validation, prospective deployment, calibration, and workflow-safe implementation remain major gaps. CONCLUSIONS: Artificial intelligence may improve diagnostic consistency, risk stratification, and early recognition of deterioration, but prospective validation and measurable clinical benefit are needed before autonomous use.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in sales (2017-early 2026): field consolidation and the rise of human-AI collaboration
items.abstract: This study examines the consolidation phase of artificial intelligence (AI) research in sales between 2017 and early 2026. Using a bibliometric analysis of Scopus data, with robustness checks across Web of Science, we identify the field’s intellectual and thematic structure during its rapid expansion. Contrary to the assumption that AI in sales primarily reflects a technological efficiency paradigm, we find three structural shifts. First, predictive analytics remains foundational but is increasingly embedded in human-AI collaboration. Second, interactional and trust-related themes move from peripheral to central, indicating a shift from performance optimization toward socio-technical integration. Third, legitimacy pressures such as transparency and corporate digital responsibility emerge as organizing dimensions rather than auxiliary concerns. Applying the TOE framework to explain these shifts across technological, organizational, and environmental dimensions, this study clarifies how AI in sales evolves through layering rather than replacement. The findings provide a research agenda for AI-enabled selling’s next phase.
